feature:hooks.reason: Hooks run on the caller's own machine, so the server has no call to refuse; it publishes the switch and the CLI and desktop honour it.

code:allowMcpServers.reason: Code sessions only: these keys govern the MCP servers a Code session starts on the caller's own machine, through the agi runtime (the CLI, and VS Code over its local agi runtime), which refuses a server the workspace turned off or whose host is not listed (apps/cli/src/cloud/workspace_policy.rs mcp_server_refusal). A signed-in account with no verified policy fails closed unless a fresh tier read shows a personal plan, and a hand-edited policy cache is ignored. This local enforcement is advisory: it binds the shipped clients, not a person who controls the machine. The shipped Electron desktop app starts no local MCP servers (the internal Tauri build is not a shipped surface and does not enforce these keys), and a cloud Code session configures none, so the server has no call to refuse. Chat connectors, including remote MCP connectors, answer to the separate connector admin allowlist (allowedConnectors, apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/connector-policy/route.ts), enforced on the server.
